architecture.mechanism: Molybdenum and chromium additions modify the microstructure of white cast iron, enhancing its resistance to abrasive wear and corrosive environments by promoting the formation of hard carbides and stabilizing the matrix.
architecture.intervention: Optimize the chromium-molybdenum ratio in the white-iron impeller composition to maximize carbide formation while maintaining matrix stability for the specific pH 2.5 slurry conditions.
architecture.expected_effect: Extended impeller service life beyond 1100 hours by improving resistance to both hydro-abrasive erosion and localized corrosion in acidic slurry.
architecture.falsification_test: Compare wear rates of impellers with modified chromium-molybdenum ratios against current standard in identical slurry conditions with pH 2.5 and 40% solids content, measuring weight loss and time to failure.
